result.title: When Does Feedback Help? Auditing Learned Voltage-Clamp Experimental Design
result.comment: Accepted as a poster at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Agentic AI for Biological Discovery (AgenticLS). 5 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables
result.summary: A learned scientific controller can outperform a misspecified planner without benefiting from feedback. We audit two synthetic voltage-clamp tasks with a training-selected fixed protocol, current masking, a Bayesian reference, and an excluded target. Five recurrent policies repeat one fixed protocol in all 1,200 off-grid rollouts; masking current changes no decision. In a crossed four-hypothesis task, a fixed diagnostic pulse is followed by one learned choice. Policies then use the first current, but tie a correctly specified Bayesian controller, and a fitted threshold reproduces the learned actions without being that controller. The excluded-target prediction gain is $4.6991\times10^{-6}$ nats per sample. Feedback use and protocol quality are separate tests. These cases establish neither biological discovery nor general RL superiority.

AI.brief_summary: 论文审计两个合成电压钳实验设计任务中的学习控制器，借助固定协议、电流掩蔽、贝叶斯参考和排除目标，检验策略是否真正利用反馈，以及协议质量是否可与之分离。
AI.relevance_reason: 其电流掩蔽、固定协议对照与阈值拟合审计，可能为判断 VLM 推理是否真正使用视觉证据、区分反馈利用与策略质量提供可借鉴的检验思路。
